title: Dilation-Covariant Hankel Pencils for Multiscale Recovery of Sparse Mellin Spectra
summary: We study sparse Mellin spectral recovery from geometric samples. Dilation covariance is shown to generate the Hankel structure directly, rather than only after reduction to a classical exponential-sum model. For complex exponents, incommensurate sampling scales remove the logarithmic aliasing that persists at a single scale. A second recovery channel is obtained from the minimal Hankel pencil: contour winding counts spectral nodes regionally, while Rouché-type bounds certify isolated nodes and unresolved clusters under noise.
